chalisa.do1: I bow to the goddess with the vīṇā in her hand: come and give me knowledge, so that, gaining understanding, I may tell the life of Ravidāsa.
chalisa.do2: The Mother's glory is boundless; this servant cannot write it. So I have come to your refuge: fulfil the hope of your devotee.
chalisa.cau1: Victory to you, Ravidāsa; have mercy, benefactor of the devotees of Hari. ॥1॥
chalisa.cau2: The devotee Rāhū was your father, and your mother was named Karmā. ॥2॥
chalisa.cau3: Their home was Māḍur near Kāśī; they made their living in a caste held untouchable. ॥3॥
chalisa.cau4: When you reached the age of twelve, devotion to Hari filled your heart. ॥4॥
chalisa.cau5: You were called a disciple of Rāmānanda, and gaining knowledge, you made your name grow. ॥5॥
chalisa.cau6: You debated the scriptures in Kāśī and taught the learned. ॥6॥
chalisa.cau7: You were a devotee of Mother Gaṅgā beyond measure; you gave the paṇḍita a cowrie as an offering. ॥7॥
chalisa.cau8: The paṇḍita took it away and offered it to Mother Gaṅgā. ॥8॥
chalisa.cau9: She stretched out her hand and took it before all, and told the boundless glory of the devotee. ॥9॥
chalisa.cau10: The paṇḍitas of Kāśī were astonished to see this deed of hers who destroys the fear of worldly existence. ॥10॥
chalisa.cau11: Then she gave a bracelet studded with gems, and made Ravidāsa its rightful owner. ॥11॥
chalisa.cau12: Gaṅgā said: Paṇḍita, give this to my devotee, who has been my servant from his first birth. ॥12॥
chalisa.cau13: The paṇḍita reached Ravidāsa, gave him the bracelet and fulfilled his wish. ॥13॥
chalisa.cau14: Then Ravidāsa said this: Dear sir, bring a second bracelet. ॥14॥
chalisa.cau15: Then the paṇḍita swore an oath: Mother Gaṅgā did not give a second. ॥15॥
chalisa.cau16: Then Ravidāsa spoke, and all the paṇḍitas were glad. ॥16॥
chalisa.cau17: He said: If the mind stays always pure, then Mother Gaṅgā dwells in the house. ॥17॥
chalisa.cau18: Then he put his hand into the wooden tub and drew out a second bracelet. ॥18॥
chalisa.cau19: He left the paṇḍitas abashed at heart, and they each went their own way. ॥19॥
chalisa.cau20: Since then a saying has been current: if the mind is pure, the Gaṅgā is in the wooden tub. ॥20॥
chalisa.cau21: Once again a dispute arose; the paṇḍitas joined together and devised a game. ॥21॥
chalisa.cau22: He whose Śālagrāma floats on the Gaṅgā, he alone shall be called a mighty devotee. ॥22॥
chalisa.cau23: All went to the bank of the Gaṅgā to float their images on the water. ॥23॥
chalisa.cau24: Everyone's sank in mid-stream; boundless sorrow filled everyone's mind. ॥24॥
chalisa.cau25: The stone image stayed afloat; gods and men together raised a cry of victory. ॥25॥
chalisa.cau26: Your name, Ravidāsa, was upheld; an outcry arose in the city. ॥26॥
chalisa.cau27: You cut open your body and made milk flow, and showed the sacred thread you were born with. ॥27॥
chalisa.cau28: Seeing it, all the men and women were astonished; the learned lost all their wits. ॥28॥
chalisa.cau29: You debated knowledge with Kabīra and astonished even him. ॥29॥
chalisa.cau30: You gave instruction to Guru Gorakha; he saw you were a saint apart and accepted it. ॥30॥
chalisa.cau31: Sadanā Pīr argued at length; you gave him instruction. ॥31॥
chalisa.cau32: Sadanā the butcher was defeated at heart, and he told the news in Delhi. ॥32॥
chalisa.cau33: Hearing that the Muslim faith had been belittled, Sikandar Lodī flew into a rage. ॥33॥
chalisa.cau34: Then he summoned you to his house and urged you to become a Muslim. ॥34॥
chalisa.cau35: You did not heed his words, and passed nights in prison. ॥35॥
chalisa.cau36: Ravidāsa had a vision of Kṛṣṇa; all your hopes were fulfilled. ॥36॥
chalisa.cau37: The locks broke and the prison opened; you struck down Sikandar's pride. ॥37॥
chalisa.cau38: He had you taken to the city of Kāśī, giving you majesty, honour and greatness. ॥38॥
chalisa.cau39: Mīrā and Yogāvatī made you their guru; they were of an eminent kṣatriya line. ॥39॥
chalisa.cau40: Giving them boundless instruction, you delivered them from worldly existence. ॥40॥
chalisa.do3: In this way Ravidāsa performed boundless deeds; however much any poet sings, even then he cannot reach their end.
chalisa.do4: If a devotee of Hari holds this Chālīsā in meditation with due observance, the Master of the world, the Lord of the universe, will protect him.
